title: CTS Practical Theology — Unit 7: Spiritual Disciplines: Solitude, Silence, Confession, and Service

blocks.en: 🌱 Practical Theology — Unit 7: Spiritual Disciplines: Solitude, Silence, Confession, and Service
blocks.es_reference: 🌱 Teología Práctica — Unidad 7: Las Disciplinas Espirituales: Soledad, Silencio, Confesión y Servicio

blocks.en: Professors: Dr. Wayne Cook & Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesores: Dr. Wayne Cook y Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: Introduction: The Inner Disciplines
blocks.es_reference: Introducción: Las Disciplinas Interiores

blocks.en: So far we have walked with God, kept a daily time with Him, learned to pray, and fed on His Word. In this unit we gather up several other practices that have shaped the people of God in every age. We will look at four: solitude, silence, confession, and service. A spiritual discipline is simply a practice we take up to make room for God's grace to do its work in the inner life. It is important to say plainly what these disciplines are not: they are not a ladder by which we climb up to God, and they are not coins with which we buy His favor. "For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast" (Ephesians 2:8–9, NKJV). We are already saved by grace through faith. The disciplines are the practices through which we seek deeper fellowship with God, more consistent obedience, and greater growth in the sanctification He is already working in us.
blocks.es_reference: Hasta aquí hemos andado con Dios, guardado un tiempo diario con Él, aprendido a orar, y nos hemos alimentado de su Palabra. En esta unidad reunimos otras prácticas que han formado al pueblo de Dios en toda época. Veremos cuatro: la soledad, el silencio, la confesión y el servicio. Una disciplina espiritual es sencillamente una práctica que adoptamos para dar lugar a que la gracia de Dios haga su obra en la vida interior. Es importante decir con claridad lo que estas disciplinas no son: no son una escalera por la cual subimos hasta Dios, ni monedas con las cuales compramos su favor. "Porque por gracia sois salvos por medio de la fe; y esto no de vosotros, pues es don de Dios; no por obras, para que nadie se gloríe" (Efesios 2:8–9, RVG). Ya somos salvos por gracia por medio de la fe. Las disciplinas son las prácticas por las cuales buscamos una comunión más profunda con Dios, una obediencia más constante, y un mayor crecimiento en la santificación que Él ya está obrando en nosotros.

blocks.en: I. Solitude — Being Alone with God
blocks.es_reference: I. La Soledad — Estar a Solas con Dios

blocks.en: Our Lord, who had every reason to be surrounded by people, made a habit of getting away to be alone with His Father. "Now in the morning, having risen a long while before daylight, He went out and departed to a solitary place; and there He prayed" (Mark 1:35, NKJV). Luke tells us this was not a single event but a pattern: "So He Himself often withdrew into the wilderness and prayed" (Luke 5:16, NKJV). Solitude is the deliberate choice to step away from noise, crowds, and even good company, so that for a time there is no one in the room but God and ourselves. In a world of constant phones and constant talking, this is harder than it sounds, and more needful than ever. The believer who never gets alone with God will find his soul crowded out.
blocks.es_reference: Nuestro Señor, que tenía toda razón para estar rodeado de gente, tenía la costumbre de apartarse para estar a solas con su Padre. "Y levantándose muy de mañana, aún muy oscuro, salió y se fue a un lugar desierto, y allí oraba" (Marcos 1:35, RVG). Lucas nos dice que esto no fue un solo suceso sino un hábito: "Mas él se apartaba a los desiertos, y oraba" (Lucas 5:16, RVG). La soledad es la decisión deliberada de alejarse del ruido, de las multitudes, y aun de la buena compañía, para que por un tiempo no haya nadie en el cuarto sino Dios y nosotros. En un mundo de teléfonos y conversación constante, esto es más difícil de lo que parece, y más necesario que nunca. El creyente que nunca se aparta a solas con Dios hallará su alma ahogada.

blocks.en: II. Silence — Stilling the Soul to Listen
blocks.es_reference: II. El Silencio — Aquietar el Alma para Escuchar

blocks.en: Closely joined to solitude is silence. Solitude removes the people; silence removes the noise of our own words. "Be still, and know that I am God" (Psalm 46:10, NKJV). "But the Lord is in His holy temple. Let all the earth keep silence before Him" (Habakkuk 2:20, NKJV). We are often afraid of quiet. We rush to fill every pause with words, even in prayer. But prayer is a conversation, and a conversation requires that we also listen. Silence is the discipline of quieting the soul long enough to hear what God has already said in His Word, and to let it sink down into the heart. "It is good that one should hope and wait quietly for the salvation of the Lord" (Lamentations 3:26, NKJV).
blocks.es_reference: Estrechamente unido a la soledad está el silencio. La soledad quita a las personas; el silencio quita el ruido de nuestras propias palabras. "Estad quietos, y conoced que yo soy Dios" (Salmo 46:10, RVG). "Mas Jehová está en su santo templo: calle delante de él toda la tierra" (Habacuc 2:20, RVG). A menudo tememos al silencio. Nos apresuramos a llenar cada pausa con palabras, aun en la oración. Pero la oración es una conversación, y una conversación requiere que también escuchemos. El silencio es la disciplina de aquietar el alma lo suficiente para oír lo que Dios ya ha dicho en su Palabra, y dejar que descienda al corazón. "Bueno es esperar en silencio la salvación de Jehová" (Lamentaciones 3:26, RVG).

blocks.en: III. Confession — Honesty About Sin
blocks.es_reference: III. La Confesión — Honestidad Acerca del Pecado

blocks.en: Confession is the discipline of refusing to hide our sin. David learned what happens when we cover it: "When I kept silent, my bones grew old through my groaning all the day long... my vitality was turned into the drought of summer" (Psalm 32:3–4, NKJV). Only when he confessed did the burden lift. Scripture gives us both a vertical and a horizontal confession. Vertically, to God: "If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness" (1 John 1:9, NKJV). Horizontally, to trusted believers: "Confess your trespasses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed" (James 5:16, NKJV). "He who covers his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and forsakes them will have mercy" (Proverbs 28:13, NKJV). Confession is not a feeling that drifts over us; it is a deliberate, humbling honesty before God and, where wise, before a brother or sister.
blocks.es_reference: La confesión es la disciplina de negarnos a esconder nuestro pecado. David aprendió lo que sucede cuando lo encubrimos: "Mientras callé, se envejecieron mis huesos en mi gemir todo el día... se volvió mi verdor en sequedades de verano" (Salmo 32:3–4, RVG). Solo cuando confesó se levantó la carga. La Escritura nos da una confesión vertical y una horizontal. Verticalmente, a Dios: "Si confesamos nuestros pecados, él es fiel y justo para perdonar nuestros pecados, y limpiarnos de toda maldad" (1 Juan 1:9, RVG). Horizontalmente, a creyentes de confianza: "Confesaos vuestras faltas unos a otros, y orad los unos por los otros, para que seáis sanados" (Santiago 5:16, RVG). "El que encubre sus pecados, no prosperará; mas el que los confiesa y se aparta, alcanzará misericordia" (Proverbios 28:13, RVG). La confesión no es un sentimiento que nos arrastra; es una honestidad deliberada y humillante delante de Dios y, donde sea sabio, delante de un hermano o hermana.

blocks.en: IV. Service — The Discipline That Turns Outward
blocks.es_reference: IV. El Servicio — La Disciplina que Mira hacia Afuera

blocks.en: The first three disciplines draw us inward and upward; service turns us outward toward others. It is the discipline that guards us from a private, self-absorbed religion. Our Lord defined greatness by it: "Whoever desires to become great among you shall be your servant... For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life a ransom for many" (Mark 10:43–45, NKJV). On the last night, He took a towel and washed the feet of His disciples, then said, "You also ought to wash one another's feet" (John 13:14, NKJV). Paul commands the same: "Through love serve one another" (Galatians 5:13, NKJV). Service practiced as a discipline keeps the heart soft and humble, and it is one of the surest cures for pride.
blocks.es_reference: Las primeras tres disciplinas nos llevan hacia adentro y hacia arriba; el servicio nos vuelve hacia afuera, hacia los demás. Es la disciplina que nos guarda de una religión privada y egoísta. Nuestro Señor definió la grandeza por ella: "El que quisiere hacerse grande entre vosotros, será vuestro servidor... Porque el Hijo del hombre no vino para ser servido, mas para servir, y dar su vida en rescate por muchos" (Marcos 10:43–45, RVG). En la última noche, tomó una toalla y lavó los pies de sus discípulos, y luego dijo: "Vosotros también debéis lavaros los pies los unos a los otros" (Juan 13:14, RVG). Pablo manda lo mismo: "Servíos por amor los unos a los otros" (Gálatas 5:13, RVG). El servicio practicado como disciplina mantiene el corazón blando y humilde, y es una de las curas más seguras para el orgullo.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión

blocks.en: Solitude, silence, confession, and service are not the property of monks or of unusually spiritual people; they are means of grace for every believer. Take them up not to be admired, and not to earn what Christ has already purchased, but to grow closer to the God who has already saved you. The danger is always to turn a discipline into a performance, or into a debt God owes us. Guard against that. Practiced humbly, in dependence on the Spirit, these disciplines quietly shape the inner life until it begins to look more like the Lord we love.
blocks.es_reference: La soledad, el silencio, la confesión y el servicio no son propiedad de los monjes ni de personas extraordinariamente espirituales; son medios de gracia para todo creyente. Adóptelos no para ser admirado, ni para ganar lo que Cristo ya compró, sino para acercarse al Dios que ya lo salvó. El peligro siempre es convertir una disciplina en una actuación, o en una deuda que Dios nos debe. Guárdese de eso. Practicadas con humildad, en dependencia del Espíritu, estas disciplinas forman calladamente la vida interior hasta que comienza a parecerse más al Señor que amamos.

sa.prompt: What is a spiritual discipline, and does practicing it earn God's favor? Explain.
sa.model: A spiritual discipline is a practice we take up to make room for God's grace to do its work in the inner life. Practicing it does NOT earn God's favor; we are already saved by grace through faith as the gift of God (Ephesians 2:8-9), so the disciplines are practices through which we seek deeper fellowship, obedience, and growth in the sanctification already at work in us, not payments toward a salvation we must win.

sa.prompt: From Mark 1:35 and Luke 5:16, what example did Jesus give about solitude?
sa.model: Jesus rose a long while before daylight and departed to a solitary place to pray (Mark 1:35), and Luke tells us this was not a single event but a pattern — He often withdrew into the wilderness to pray (Luke 5:16). His example shows that even the Lord, who had every reason to be surrounded by people, made a deliberate habit of getting alone with the Father.

sa.prompt: What is the discipline of silence, and why do we need it in prayer?
sa.model: Silence is the discipline of quieting the soul long enough to listen — stilling not just our surroundings but our own words. We need it in prayer because prayer is a conversation, and a conversation requires that we also listen, rather than rushing to fill every pause with our own talking, as Psalm 46:10 says: 'Be still, and know that I am God.'

sa.prompt: According to Psalm 32 and 1 John 1:9, what happens when we hide sin versus confess it?
sa.model: When David kept silent about his sin, his bones grew old through groaning and his vitality dried up (Psalm 32:3-4); only when he confessed did the burden lift. 1 John 1:9 promises that if we confess our sins, God is faithful and just to forgive us and cleanse us from all unrighteousness — hiding sin brings misery, but honest confession brings forgiveness and cleansing.

sa.prompt: What does James 5:16 teach about confession to one another?
sa.model: James 5:16 teaches us to confess our trespasses to one another, and to pray for one another, that we may be healed. This horizontal confession, to trusted believers, is meant to bring healing and accountability, alongside our vertical confession directly to God.

sa.prompt: How did Jesus define greatness in Mark 10:43-45, and how did He show it in John 13?
sa.model: Jesus said whoever desires to be great among us must be a servant, for even the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve and give His life a ransom for many (Mark 10:43-45). He showed this concretely in John 13 by taking a towel and washing His disciples' feet, an act of humble service, then telling them to do the same for one another.

sa.prompt: Why is service called a discipline that turns the heart outward?
sa.model: Service is called a discipline that turns the heart outward because the first three disciplines draw us inward and upward, while service turns us toward others, guarding against a private, self-absorbed religion. Practiced as a discipline, service keeps the heart soft and humble, and it is one of the surest cures for pride.

sa.prompt: Why are the disciplines NOT a way to earn salvation? Use Ephesians 2:8-9.
sa.model: The disciplines are NOT a way to earn salvation because Ephesians 2:8-9 says we have been saved by grace through faith, not of ourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast. Since salvation is already a gift received by faith in Christ, the disciplines cannot add to it — they are the fruit of a salvation already given, not the price of one still owed.

sa.prompt: What is the danger the unit warns about when practicing the disciplines?
sa.model: The unit warns against turning a discipline into a performance for others to admire, or into a debt God owes us because we practiced it. The danger is treating solitude, silence, confession, or service as ways to impress people or to earn something from God, rather than as humble means of grace practiced quietly before Him.

sa.prompt: In your own words, what do solitude, silence, confession, and service have in common?
sa.model: Solitude, silence, confession, and service all have in common that they are disciplines — practices that make room for God's grace to shape the inner life. None of them earns God's favor; all of them are means by which a believer already saved by grace grows closer to God and is gradually formed to look more like Christ.
